title: Read a Group with Its Own Closing Marker

blocks.text: Grouping Records Changes What It Means to Finish

The format of one group starts with { group NAME, contains zero or more records, and ends with }. Each record has an ID from 0..9 followed by a Recuento [aceptados;rechazados], with quantities from 0..10. Valid names are red, green, and blue. Example: { group red 7[0;0] 2[3;1] }. An ID cannot repeat within the group, and record order is preserved.

Labels and names are read as strings using >>, so whitespace must separate them from the next token. Thus { group red } permits an empty group, but { group red} does not belong to this format: the name would be read as red}. Whitespace may be spaces, tabs, or newlines skipped by ordinary stream extraction. No whitespace is required between an ID and [; quantities are read as decimal integers, allowing a + sign and leading zeros. This reader recognizes only the format described.

blocks.question: A reader has started { group red and reaches EOF after 7[2;1], without }. What is the result for that group?
options: Valid, because the record is complete.
Valid if the stream has eofbit.
Invalid: the group that started has not been closed.
blocks.explanation: EOF ends the character source. It does not complete an object that is still missing its closing marker.

blocks.text: leer_grupo receives a borrowed stream and a Grupo destination. It returns true after consuming exactly one complete group; it neither requires EOF nor consumes anything after }. On false, it preserves the destination but does not return previously consumed characters to the stream. A domain or label rejection may also leave the stream without failbit: rely on this function's bool. These exercises use fresh streams with their usual settings: decimal extraction, whitespace skipping, and no added exception mask. The reader does not automatically adapt a stream configured in another way.
Look for the Closing Marker Before Attempting Another Record

The earlier full-line reader required nothing to remain after its Registro. That does not work here: after a record there may be another record or }. We reuse the Recuento operator>> and check the ID separately. To detect a closing marker, we skip whitespace with ws and inspect the next character using peek(). peek() observes without extracting; get() consumes a character once we decide to do so.

blocks.question: Predict the output. This example has already checked that characters are available.
blocks.explanation: peek observed }, but get extracted it. The following string remains available.

blocks.text: Before peek, the reader must check !entrada and entrada.eof() after ws. If a closing marker is no longer available, it returns false. It does not clear the state of a malformed record to treat it as a permitted end: an actual closing marker differs from a failed extraction.

blocks.question: After skipping whitespace, the next character is [ where the ID of another Registro was expected. What should the reader do?
options: Attempt to extract the record, then reject it because no valid ID is obtained.
Treat any extraction failure as if } had been seen.
Clear the state and save a record with an initial ID of 0.
blocks.explanation: Only } is the permitted closing marker. A failed extraction does not create a record or justify accepting the group.

blocks.text: Build a Candidate and Protect the Destination

Define leer_grupo. Check the opening character, label, name, and group ID. Prepare a new Grupo candidate with no records. On each iteration: skip whitespace; reject if the stream cannot continue or reached EOF; consume } and accept the candidate if it is the next character; otherwise read a new Registro, check its ID and ensure it is not already present in that candidate, then append it. Do not modify the destination until the closing marker is recognized.

Build four tests with an initial blue destination containing 9[1;1]: a red group with 7[0;0] and 2[3;1]; an empty green group; red with ID 7 repeated; and red with one complete record but no closing marker. Display bool:group_ID:record_count followed by the records obtained. Predict before running.
The next page contains the reference. The exercise is to build the reader's control flow, not to copy a complete body. The model preserves zero as a valid value and an empty group as present.
Later Reference: The Closing Marker Confirms the Candidate

The expected lines are 1:0:2 7[0;0] 2[3;1], 1:1:0, 0:2:1 9[1;1], and 0:2:1 9[1;1]. The empty group replaces the destination with a valid group containing no records. Both rejections preserve the entire previous group, even if an initial valid record had already been read.

Criteria: fresh state for each read, duplicates checked within their group, exact closing marker, domains checked before using data, order preserved, and destination unchanged on false. Also test quantities -1 and 11, IDs -1 and 10, an unknown name, a different label, and an input truncated at every field of the first record. A semantic rejection is not required to set stream failure flags.

A valid iteration consumes a record; the closing marker ends the group; failure rejects it. In addition, there are only ten distinct permitted IDs in a group. This bound does not replace environmental limits on time, memory, or the length of character input.
A Complete Group Is Not Yet a Complete Test File

blocks.question: Predict the output. leer_grupo consumes only the group and leaves the remainder to the caller.
blocks.explanation: The empty blue group is valid; remainder is still available. Validation of the full test file must decide whether that suffix is allowed.

blocks.question: Record 7[0;0] was read successfully in red. Then 7[3;1] appears in a new blue group. Which duplicate check is appropriate?
options: Look up the ID across all previous groups and reject it.
Do not check duplicates because the name is already valid.
Look up the ID within the current blue candidate.
blocks.explanation: A record's identity includes its group. The outer collection will check that the group itself is not repeated.

blocks.text: Transfer: insert newlines between records and a suffix after }. The first change preserves the data; the group reader leaves the suffix unread. Removing } must cause rejection even when quantities and IDs are valid. In the next lesson, the caller will have its own closing marker.
Reading structures is discussed in the primary source (Stroustrup, 2024, sections 9.8–9.9.2, pp. 267–274). The grammar, guarantees, and exercises are original to this learning path.
